title: UDP: Utility-Driven Fetch Directed Instruction Prefetching
problem: Datacenter applications exhibit large instruction footprints causing significant instruction cache misses and frontend stalls. Existing fetch-directed instruction prefetching mechanisms remain far from ideal, with inaccurate and untimely prefetches hiding up to 588.47% of potential IPC speedup.
motivation: Reducing frontend stalls through improved instruction prefetching accuracy and timeliness is critical for unlocking substantial performance gains in datacenter processors.
method: UDP and UFTQ mechanisms enhance fetch-directed instruction prefetching (FDIP) accuracy without compromising timeliness through utility-driven feedback that adapts to application-specific characteristics. The approach leverages prefetches on the wrong path and uses utility metrics to guide prefetch decisions, requiring only 8 KB of storage and moderate hardware modifications.
key_novelty: Utility-driven adaptive instruction prefetching that maintains accuracy and timeliness while exploiting wrong-path prefetches to improve instruction cache hit rates.
contributions: Quantifies gap between existing FDIP implementations and ideal instruction caching with detailed characterization of accuracy vs. timeliness tradeoffs
Proposes UDP mechanism for application-specific, utility-driven prefetch accuracy improvement
Introduces UFTQ mechanism to maintain timeliness while improving accuracy
Achieves 16.1% max IPC and 3.6% average IPC improvement with practical 8 KB overhead

metrics.speedup: 16.1% maximum IPC improvement, 3.6% average IPC improvement

limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations in the provided abstract
